clears: mac-bench 7c0bba2, the #44 start-race gate. It touches BoardDevice.read() and this test reads first_seq, so it was worth excluding rather than assuming: 11 of 11 pass uncontended on the commit that carries it.
failure_shape: gaps at the reading client, 1 to 11 per failing run, first_seq 0. windows-desk saw 1 gap with first_seq 5.
means: The test is CPU-contention sensitive on macOS as well as Windows. It saturates the daemon at preset 5 with a wedged client and the fan-out is Python, so a starved reader thread drops frames for the healthy client - which is what the test asserts must not happen.
not_claimed: That the test is wrong. A client falling behind must not cost another its data, and that is the right assertion. What is shown is only that its margin does not survive a saturated host, so a failure of it is not evidence about the device unless the bench was idle.
why: windows-desk hit 1 failed / 577 passed on a full Track B run and attributed it to their own CPU contention - they had run a 55 s board-free pytest in the same window. That is a hypothesis about a mechanism, not just a failure to reproduce, and a mechanism can be tested directly on another platform.
